proposal: When the first complete native-validated segment of an initially approved YouTube recording is committed, associate its existing approximate wall origin with its native parsed source_start. Retain a typed, opaque native continuation context; do not accept a browser-supplied arbitrary wall-time anchor.

Issue the context only through an approved format-boundary finalization after any validated tail is committed. Bind it to the exact receiver, canonical live/video identity, sourceId, document generation, full RecordingOwner and current recording intent. An implicit receiver-wide cache is insufficient because a later manual start must not inherit an old run. A zero-progress boundary without an established anchor must not fabricate one.

Consume that context once at the fresh native-approved successor admission under the existing arm/owner/cancel fences. At its first validated segment derive successorOriginMs=originalOriginMs+round((successorSourceStart-originalSourceStart)*1000), not from delayed successor commit time. Preserve the original reference anchor across further successors so repeated rounding or wait time does not accumulate drift.

Require finite validated source intervals, checked millisecond arithmetic and plausible wall time. A source clock reset, mismatched identity/owner/epoch, missing proof, or adjacent source discontinuity beyond the current250ms continuity acceptance must not silently reuse the affine relationship. Keep valid video and retained chat, but expose missing/uncertain timing and partial coverage rather than manufacture synchronization. Do not clamp media timestamps or weaken mux validation.

Write a bounded version2 YouTube-only chat-timeline document containing the explicit derived media origin and its fixed anchor-method classification while preserving the truthful firstSegmentCommittedAtMs and actual duration. timelineQuality remains receive-time-approximate. The reader accepts the version2 origin only with valid provider/method/version/ranges; malformed/unsupported version2 must not fall back to the delayed version1 formula. Existing version1/SOOP reading stays unchanged. No previously saved user's timeline is rewritten.

Add bounded metadata to the existing YouTube recent buffer indicating the time/coverage of evicted rows. Prefer already-parsed source timestamps used by replay; retain conservative host-receive/unknown coverage for raw or untimed rows. Do not log row contents. At archive attachment snapshot only losses that precede that attachment; later eviction of rows already written to the active archive is not an archive loss.

Once the actual replay origin is established, compare the attachment's loss snapshot with the required media interval. If dropped coverage may overlap, retain existing originals and mark the archive partial with existing ArchiveLimit; uncertain timing/coverage uses StatusUnknown. An old loss entirely before a new recording's required interval must not permanently poison all later archives. Raw protocol/status-only rows with proven no replay content should not invent chat loss. A verified quiet stream with zero chat and no overlapping loss remains complete.

Bind any coverage-resolution call to the exact active archive marker/job so late first-segment or old-finalizer work cannot mutate a successor. Preserve earlier Interrupted/WriteFailed/FlushFailed/ArchiveLimit reasons; do not replace a known failure with Complete. Missing origin at detach remains honest unknown/partial. Video verification and durable cleanup rules remain independent of chat completeness.
